reasoning: For each index i define I_i and D_i as the maximum lengths of strictly increasing and strictly decreasing subsequences ending at i. If neither desired subsequence exists, 1<=I_i,D_i<=n. There are n^2 possible ordered pairs but n^2+1 indices, so some i<j share a pair. Distinctness gives a_i<a_j or a_i>a_j. In the first case an optimal increasing subsequence ending at i extends to j, so I_j>=I_i+1; in the second, D_j>=D_i+1. Either contradicts equality of the shared pair. This proves the exact target with no predecessors or external results.

result: The verifier accepted the complete target theorem.
